description: Single-panel grouped bar chart (no sub-panels) of specific stiffness normalised to aluminium. The ordinate is labelled "Specific stiffness/specific stiffness of Al", scaled 0 to 1.2 with tick/gridline spacing of 0.2 and no unit (it is a ratio). The abscissa carries three category groups corresponding to the load-case index of the specific-stiffness expression E^n/ρ: "E/ρ" (tie), "√E/ρ" (beam) and "∛E/ρ" (panel). Each group contains four bars, identified by the horizontal top legend as "Aluminium" (white, black outline), "HSLA" (pink hatched), "Fe-8Al" (green hatched) and "Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C" (teal hatched). The aluminium bar is the reference at the 1.0 line in every group. In the E/ρ group the HSLA bar is tallest, rising just above the 1.0 line, while Fe-8Al and Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C lie just below 1.0, with Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C lowest. For √E/ρ and ∛E/ρ all three steels drop far below the aluminium reference; Fe-8Al is marginally the taller of the HSLA/Fe-8Al pair (just above the 0.6 and 0.5 gridlines), and Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C is the shortest. No numeric data labels are printed on any bar. The figure demonstrates that the low-density Fe-Al and Fe-Mn-Al-C steels give no specific-stiffness advantage over HSLA or 6xxx aluminium.
measured_quantities: specific stiffness normalised to aluminium (dimensionless ratio), for E/ρ, √E/ρ and ∛E/ρ

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled "Specific stiffness/specific stiffness of Al" and runs from 0 to 1.2 with printed ticks every 0.2, so all bars are dimensionless ratios to aluminium.
The x-axis has three category groups labelled "E/ρ", "√E/ρ" and "∛E/ρ".
The legend lists exactly four entries: "Aluminium", "HSLA", "Fe-8Al" and "Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C".
The aluminium (white) bar is at the 1.0 line in all three groups, i.e. it is the normalisation reference.
In the E/ρ group the HSLA bar is the tallest and extends just above the 1.0 line, whereas the Fe-8Al and Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C bars lie below 1.0, with Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C the shortest of the four.

In the √E/ρ group the three steel bars fall far below the aluminium reference: HSLA and Fe-8Al sit just above the 0.6 gridline (Fe-8Al marginally taller) and Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C is the shortest, just below that level.
In the ∛E/ρ group all steel bars are just above the 0.5 gridline (Fe-8Al tallest, Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C shortest) and thus about half the aluminium value.
No numeric data labels are printed on any bar; values can only be read relative to the 0.2-spaced gridlines.
The bar ranking is the same for √E/ρ and ∛E/ρ (Fe-8Al ≳ HSLA > Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C, all below Aluminium), whereas for E/ρ the order is HSLA > Aluminium > Fe-8Al > Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C.
The caption states the figure compares the specific stiffness of Fe-8Al [24], Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C [5], HSLA and aluminium 6xxx alloys.
The citing text states that the specific-stiffness index E^n/ρ uses n = 1 for a tie, n = 1/2 for a beam and n = 1/3 for a panel, matching the three x-axis groups.

The citing text concludes from this figure that the specific stiffness of the low-density steels is not higher than that of HSLA steels and aluminium alloys, so weight saving with low-density steels requires parts not limited by stiffness.

subfigures.description: One grouped bar chart: y-axis "Specific stiffness/specific stiffness of Al" from 0 to 1.2 in 0.2 steps, x-axis with three groups labelled E/ρ, √E/ρ and ∛E/ρ, each containing four bars for Aluminium, HSLA, Fe-8Al and Fe-22Mn-8Al-0.8C, with aluminium set to 1.0 as the reference in each group.
